pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group cardiovascular outcomes study; lixisenatide 20 µg QD vs. placebo add-on to standard of care in T2DM patients with recent ACS
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to first occurrence of composite MACE+ (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina); ITT population
pivotal_trials.result: HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.89–1.17); upper bound <1.3 meeting non-inferiority; lixisenatide 406/3034 (13.4%) vs. placebo 399/3034 (13.2%) with primary MACE+ events

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized (2:1 or 3:1), placebo-controlled, parallel-group studies; lixisenatide 20 µg QD vs. placebo as monotherapy or add-on to metformin, SU, pioglitazone, or basal insulin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24 (Week 12 for monotherapy study EFC6018); primary analysis ANCOVA LOCF mITT
pivotal_trials.trial_name: GetGoal Program (9 placebo-controlled studies: EFC6018, EFC6014, EFC10743, EFC6015, EFC6017, EFC6016, EFC10781, EFC10887, EFC11321)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean HbA1c difference vs. placebo ranged from -0.25% (95% CI -0.425, -0.078) to -0.79% (95% CI -1.032, -0.552); p<0.05 in all nine studies

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, active-controlled, 3-arm parallel-group study; lixisenatide 20 µg QD vs. insulin glulisine QD vs. insulin glulisine TID on background insulin glargine ± metformin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: change from baseline in HbA1c and body weight at Week 26; ANCOVA mITT
pivotal_trials.result: HbA1c LS mean change: lixisenatide -0.63% vs. insulin glulisine QD -0.57% (difference -0.06, 95% CI -0.176, 0.061, p=0.341; non-inferior) and vs. insulin glulisine TID -0.84% (difference 0.21, 95% CI 0.094, 0.331, p=0.0005; non-inferior by pre-specified margin but statistically worse); body weight: lixisenatide -0.68 kg vs. glulisine QD +0.99 kg (difference -1.67 kg) and vs. glulisine TID +1.35 kg (difference -2.03 kg)

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, active-controlled, parallel-group study; lixisenatide 20 µg QD vs. exenatide 10 µg BID add-on to metformin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24; non-inferiority margin 0.4%; ANCOVA mITT
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean HbA1c change: lixisenatide -0.85% vs. exenatide -1.03%; LS mean difference 0.18% (95% CI 0.046, 0.307); non-inferiority demonstrated at Week 24 but lixisenatide statistically worse than exenatide (p=0.0083); non-inferiority not preserved beyond Week 36

key_safety: The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal (nausea 28% vs. 7.1% placebo, vomiting 9.8% vs. 1.8% placebo); notable safety concerns included anaphylaxis (ARAC-adjudicated: 16 [0.2%] lixisenatide vs. 5 [0.1%] placebo), high anti-drug antibody positivity (~70% by Week 24), hypoglycemia when combined with insulin or sulfonylurea (severe hypoglycemia 2.1% vs. 0.6% in long-term insulin study EFC6016), and calcitonin elevations ≥50 pg/mL (0.4% lixisenatide vs. <0.1% placebo in ELIXA).
target_moa: Selective GLP-1 receptor agonist; stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, and delays gastric emptying by binding and activating the GLP-1 receptor

_meta.indication:
ADLYXIN is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Limitations of Use:
- ADLYXIN has not been studied in patients with chronic pancreatitis or a history of unexplained pancreatitis. Consider other antidiabetic therapies in patients with a history of pancreatitis.
- ADLYXIN is not a substitute for insulin. ADLYXIN is not indicated for use in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus or for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis.
- The concurrent use of ADLYXIN with short acting insulin has not been studied and is not recommended.
- ADLYXIN has not been studied in patients with gastroparesis and is not recommended in patients with gastroparesis.

indication_details.population_restrictions: adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus; not for type 1 diabetes mellitus; not for diabetic ketoacidosis; not for patients with gastroparesis
